newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down next week.

text.p: Polish shares on Thursday extended Wednesday's gains but analysts said the dominant selling after price-fixing and mixed continuous trade signalled falls next week, with the market looking fairly valued at best.
"Polish firms look fairly valued," said Krzysztof Olszewski of Bank Slaski brokerage, referring to the market's current price earnings ratio of 15.6.

Analysts said the recent underperformance by banks, which make up about 40 percent of the main index, was caused by recent slower earnings growth compared to other heavyweights and was keeping the main index down.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 2.1 percent to 16,690.4 points and turnover rose three percent to 234.2 million zlotys ($76.2 milliion) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 73 to 10 with 10 stocks flat.

Analysts said Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw, which rose 8.7 and 7.3 percent, could continue to outperform the market next week if investors reamain confident the paintakers' planned merger will go through.
On Wednesday Cieszyn had surged and Wroclaw plunged after the firms' shareholders agreed on a merger, with Cieszyn's approving a plan giving them 53.5 percent.
Wroclaw officials have said a mutual shareholder, bank BIG, might dispute Cieszyn's version in court but the merger was still likely to go through as a delay would cost both firms.
On Thursday a Wroclaw shareholder said it and other Western investment funds had asked the Polish securities commission to prevent Cieszyn's version of the merger.
Analysts said debt-ridden Espebepe, up 9.4 percent, continued this week's speculative surge after last week's drop. The firm's creditors meet on April 14 to discuss a possible debt deal.
